OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files

From: Mr. C.A. Hubbard, WIGAN

Dear Ron and Brian,

I must thank you for including
my queries in the December issue
and I would like to thank all
the people who replied. The
feed-back was unbelievable! If
room can be found in a future
issue I'd like to thank: Les
Phillips, BLANDFORD; Les Tyler,
CHELTENHAM; MR. R. Bates,
NOTTINGHAM; Colin Demeline,
NELSON; Bob Smith, PETERBOROUGH;
MR. I.A.G. Ross, BRIDGE OF WEIR.
All of whom wrote to me and also
those who took the time and
trouble to telephone. Thanks to
you all.
           Cyril A. Hubbard

From Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH


Dear Brian,

First of all, a happy New Year
and all the best with OUTLET in
1991.

I am writing in response to your
Outletter in January's issue,
where you were asking if anyone
knew of a failsafe way to detect
128 mode after using POKE 23611,
205. I know of a method which
ought to do the trick but you'd
have to test it with Interface 1
attached to be sure as that can
alter the 'standard' system in
ways that I don't know an awful
lot about.

128 and 48 modes use a different
error return address (pointed to
by ERR SP system variables 23613
& 4), and PEEKing to see what
this address is should tell you
what mode you're in. With 48
BASIC this will usually be 4867
in the ROM(MAIN-4 routine),while
128 BASIC uses the 'ONERR'
routine in the printer buffer.

With older 128 machines ONERR
starts at 23325, while on the
+2A and +3 it is at 23354, so
the test can not only determine
the mode, but can also be used
to ascertain which type of 128K
machine is being used. This
could be useful if you needed to
use the RAMDISK etc., where the
syntax is different.

Programs could then be written
for any 128K machine, by using
both types of syntax on separate
lines and using the test to
determine which line to GO TO.

If you just want to test which
mode is being used, all you need
to PEEK is the high byte of the
error ret. address, which will
be 91 on (all) 128K machines in
128 mode (19 in 48 mode). To
determine the type of 128 BASIC,
PEEK the low byte, which will be
29 for an older machine, 58 for
a +2A/+3. The following line
might perhaps be a neat way of
doing the mode test:-

  10 LET mode=48+80*(PEEK (PEEK
  23613+256* PEEK 23614+1)=91)

The preceding line of BASIC just
gives the variable MODE a value
of either 128 or 48, indicating
in a straightforward way the
mode being used. The following
would be useful if you had a
program in which you needed to
use, say, the RAMDISK on any
128K machine:

100 LET type=PEEK(PEEK 23613+256
* PEEK 23614): IF type=29 THEN
GO TO 120:REM older 128K machine

110 CAT "M:": SAVE "M:filename"
CODE x,y: GO TO 130

120 CAT !: SAVE !"filename" CODE
x,y

130 RETURN

The only problem with the above
is you might have difficulty
entering line 120 in the first
place on a machine which uses +3
BASIC! However, I hope this
information may be of some help
to you in the future. If you
find it has any limitations I
would be pleased to know, but as
far as I can tell with my own
system (grey +2 and no Interface
1) it always works OK.
                - Miles Kinloch

Thanks Miles. Your method looks
sound and I've made a note to do
some tests with a view to using
it, where necessary, in future
OUTLET programs. MUSIC BOX, in
this issue, uses my old UDG test
but I may change it if I get
time.           - Brian Cavers

From: Les Tyler, CHELTENHAM

In reply to your query,[printing
from OUTDEX - see OUTLETTERS 41]
I normally I use a 128K Spectrum
with Multiface 128 and Disciple/
drives and use the RS232 port of
the 128 Spectrum to drive the
printer. However,if this machine
is out of action I have a 48K
with Interface 1/microdrives.

The printer is then fed from
Interface 1. I have found from
experience that, although it is
possible to operate Interface 1
behind Disciple, it is not
really very efficient when one
also has the Multiface plugged
in. The Spectrum can only take
so much, after all.

With OUTLET text files I use
COL80+ and its 'USER' option,
which calls a simple RS232
routine to drive the printer in
128 mode. This basically applies
to virtually any other printing
requirement except OUTDEX which
refuses to play ball. (As Ken
Livingstone says about your
local cheese - can't think why!)

As I use my MASTERFILE mod to
OUTDEX more than the original
nowadays, the problem is not so
much important as annoying. I
would appreciate any feedback.

MASTERFILE has had plenty of
mentions in recent OUTLETS -
clearly it's a popular utility
with many readers, including
myself, of course.

Although most files produced for
MASTERFILE will be tailored for
individual requirements, it's
probable that many will be of
interest and possible value to
others, who otherwise would not
be aware of them.

Apart from the OUTDEX file
previously reported, I have also
produced one which contains all
STD codes in numerical order,
with their exchanges, which I've
found very useful especially
when studying the adverts in
'Micro Mart' and the like where
often only a phone number is
given for the advertiser. I am
sure others have also produced
files of equal or greater value
for those other than themselves.

Perhaps they might care to make
them available via OUTBOARD or
the letters pages in OUTLET? I'd
like to know of any reaction to
this suggestion.
                 Cheers! - Les

Send our STD file, Les.It may be
possible to put it in OUTLET in
some form and would be useful.

Re: the printing problem, sorry,
I need more info! What changes
did you make to COL80 and OUTDEX
and what results did you get
(e.g., No print at all, garbage,
lock up, error message etc.)?
What syntax does the 128K RS232
use to start sending (a) printer
codes (b)the expanded Sinclair
keywords (the equivalent of the
Disciple POKE @6,1 and 0)?-Brian

From J. Jones, MANSFIELD

I have an Opus Discovery with
twin drives that seems to have a
total breakdown if I use it with
my Speccy +2 (grey) but if used
with a black 128(before Amstrad)
it works perfectly.

I have been told the regulator
is at fault. I have also been
told through CRASH magazine that
the 128 and 128 +2 have the same
insides. If this is so then I'm
totally puzzled! Can you help in
any way?
       At Breaking Point,

        Yours pleadingly,

            J. Jones

To Mr. J. Jones from Brian Gaff

A strange tale! Normally, I find
the older 128K is the one which
gives rise to add-on problems.

Firstly,the grey +2 is electron-
ically the same as the 128K. The
only difference being the ROM.
You don't say which ROM you have
in your Discovery; it may be a
simple incompatability problem.

I would not think it's anything
to do with the PSU, as any prob-
lems should also affect the 128K
unless there's a broken track in
the +2 of course!There is always
the possibility the Z80 in the
+2 may have a faulty M1 line. If
this is the problem, Interface 1
would also fail to work.

Perhaps your best bet would be
to have a chat with the S.D.C.
(Spectrum Discovery Club), who
are at:-

      57 St. Saviour's Road
          West Croydon
         Surrey CR0 2XE

                          - B.G.

FROM ANDY FLEMING, DEVIZES

May I heap my praises along with
everybody else on the brothers
Cavers for producing OUTLET and
my thanks to all their regular
contributors. I would not now
willingly forego my monthly
treat.

I would like to express an opin-
ion about Tasword in its various
forms. I looked at a few word
processors before I bought the
one I use now: 'The Last Word'.
Tasword is constantly in the
media with enhancements for it,
fixes for bugs, customizing etc.
Why bother?Go out and get a copy
of 'TLW'it's got all you'll ever
need,including its own customiz-
ing section and is cheaper.

O.K. I know Tasword was first
and occupies the same position
to the Spectrum that 'Wordstar'
does on the PCs(spit). I still
think if it didn't need fixing
so much(with the resulting media
coverage - indirect plugging?)
then maybe a more efficient pro-
gram,like 'TLW', could come more
to the fore.

When I bought'The Last Word' for
my Spectrum+2,PlusD,3.5" drives,
it was cheaper than Tasword too
- a couple of years ago now.

On the subject of SCART,I decid-
ed to get a monitor/tv a few
weeks ago and was told I could
use it with my set-up and a lead
could be obtained. As I was

getting it through a friend,with
a good staff discount, I don't
want to go into too much detail
about the retailer. Suffice to
say the set was a Sony Trinitron
as another reader recently had.

After some research the shop
said "Sorry, no commercial lead
available but we'll make you one
up."

"O.K.", says I, "no hurry"

So the staff technician was put
to work.It was not in his normal
line so therefore I had to be
content to wait and be patient.

I was.

"Sorry", says the shop, "Amstrad
say it won't work. You need an
amplifier. We'll have another
go...".

"...OK, cracked it, be with you
in a week."

A week later, "Sorry but we have
a problem getting a picture."

Three weeks later, just before
Xmas, "YIPPEE!!! We've done it.
It's all down to the length of
the lead."

I took delivery; plugged in;
BEEEUATiful - for two minutes.
Investigation revealed that some
of the soldered leads had come
adrift in the plug on the comp-
uter end of the lead.

When I can get to see the tech-
nician after Xmas I hope to get
the pin-out schematic from him
to solder up myself.

If I'm sucessful with my solder-
ing I'll let you know. It may be
others have the same problem. By
the same token I'd be grateful
for any advice. I don't want to
detract from the guy who made
the lead up as he obviously went
to a lot of trouble to research
what he did but the lead is a
bit of a bodge and I think(know)
I can do better.

                - Andy Fleming

To Andy Fleming from Brian Gaff


Thanks for your comments on word
processors. Certainly Tasword 2
is now out of date but Tasman do
make other Spectrum versions
with much better features. The
reason we tend to use Tas 2, is
that almost everyone has a copy
lying around.


ARGH!!! SCART strikes again! You
do not say if you are using the
composite or RGB connections
but I know both work OK. Quite
often RGB can look better and
if your monitor is linear RGB,
you can see BRIGHT too.

If you want sound of course, you
may have trouble. Is this what
Amstrad meant by you needing an
amp, I wonder. Personally, I
think there are leads available
for the Speccy to SCART. I think
Romantic Robot do them. Good
luck with the soldering, if you
do eventually give it a try.

                         - B.G.



[FOOTNOTE FROM B.C. - I have now
received an update from Andy
reporting success with details
which I'll put in a future DRIVE
CHAT article.]

  Dick Chappell, 36 Ravensdene
    Crescent, Belfast BT6 0DB
        (Tel:0232 648321)


Dear Ron and Brian,

I've heard a whisper that Carol
Brooksbank will soon be putting
the finishing touches to a book
on the SAM graphics program,
FLASH.  This is good news indeed
for the SAM population.

Carol is frequently mentioned in
OUTLET, always with the greatest
respect for her programming
skills.  The clarity with which
she presents her work ensures
that beginner and experienced
programmer alike can benefit.

Her "Small is beautiful" program
for printing out screen dumps of
varying sizes appeared in FORMAT
for both SPECTRUM and (later)SAM
COUPE. The many who took trouble
to key it in found it a little
gem of a utility. I will be in
the queue for any treatment of
"FLASH" that comes from her pen.

My address and 'phone number are
FREEWARE! When I move to the
mainland in the not-too-distant
future, I shall send an update.

With every issue I continue to
be impressed not only by the
quality of the majority of
contributions, but above all by
the professionalism with which
you present them, adding your

own expertise to make a well -
rounded product... and for so
many different configurations!

May you continue to make light
of your not inconsiderable
problems in the year ahead! But
please don't add to them by
lightly extending the workload
with new undertakings. Forgive
my intruding here...you know
best what are your strengths and
your limitations...but there
must be others of your readers
who, like me, sometimes wonder
how you can keep it all going so
smoothly. (I'm touching wood!)
Just you all take care, now!
Switch off once in a while.
                - Dick Chappell

Many thanks, Dick.     - B.C.

From Brian Gaff



SC_ASSEMBLER mis-assembles IY
instructions as IX. This bug can
be fixed by...


  FOR A =73794 TO 73818 STEP 4

  POKE A,253

  NEXT A

From: Adam Inglis, SHREWSBURY

Why do you remove the non-
convertible Spectrum programs
from the SAM disc as many SAM
users (with Spectrums) have
utilities (SPECMAKER, SAMTape,
SAMCo Emulators etc.) which
could be used to run the
Spectrum programs and code.

In issue 039 Paul Oliver said
the 'frontend' programs wouldn't
LOAD-IN another non AUTO -
LOADing program; this can be
overcome on the SAM by typing
in: LOAD '--FILENAME--' LINE X
[WHERE --FILENAME-- IS THE NAME
OF THE PROGRAM AND X IS THE LINE
NUMBER]- just like SAVEing and
auto-loading programs.

In issue 039 - 'LABELLER' does
not work with my SAM.  Is it
supposed to?
                - ADAM INGLIS

No -I couldn't convert it easily
but must have accidentally left
my attempt on the OUTLET disc.

Your LOAD""LINE is a very useful
tip and also STOPS auto-run pro-
grams running with LOAD "NAME"
LINE 62000...!!

If there's room I may put some
of the Spectrum programs that
won't convert on the SAM disc. I
am very doubtful you can do much
with some of them but best of
luck - and let me know!
                        - Brian

From: C.M. HOWELL.

Dear Sirs,

Re: Brian's comment in OUTLET 40
that a +D will only work in 48k
mode on a +2A. I recently tested
a +D and +2A with an adaptor
from DATEL ELECTRONICS. I found
that if you enter 128 BASIC,
press EDIT and select SCREEN$
the +D works as it should. This
is the same with the 128+ and
the +2 both of which I own. This
is explained on page 3 of the
Users' Manual.
                  - C.M.HOWELL

Thanks. I assume the "adaptor"
you mention is the TWO-FACE"?
                      - Brian C.

From: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON.


Issue 40 was the first OUTLET I
have seen.  Looking at it, well,
what can I say? Much better than
SOME of the offerings I have
encountered in the past. AT LAST
a mag. where the people are
(fairly) sane, know what they're
talking about, and don't waffle
on about why the Amiga is better
than the ST and vice-versa!

Incidentally, I think I recog-
nised Bob Smith from one of the
better offerings. (Until the
editor changed). Was he known as
the Bos'un? I am sorry to bring
this up, but the curiosity is
killing me!

Can I nitpick at a few of the
things in Issue 40?  The first
is the address George North gave
for Maplin.  Although this is
partly correct as it is the
address of one of their shops.
In their catalogue they say all
mail should be sent to them at
PO Box 3,Rayleigh,Essex,SS6 8LR.
If you want more info, you can
buy their catalogue from your
local W.H. Smith for `2.45. If
you choose not to, however, bear
in mind that they charge `1 for
handling on all orders.

I now use a Logitech PC scanner
on my PC at work (as mentioned
in Issue 40).  It comes with a
plug-in interface board and
driver software for a PC but is
NOT directly RS232-compatible.

I think this may be the same one
mentioned. (Mine's ScanMan+).The
interface board is quite complex
and it would probably be quite
difficult to conjure up a Speccy
version of it. I don't think it
would be easy to modify the
existing board correctly. It has
DIP switches to change between
different interrupt vectors that
the TSR driver uses.

Most people won't know what I'm
talking about - I did warn you
it was complex!  I won't go into
any more detail but suffice to
say that it may be an idea to
check before you part with your
money.Can anyone provide me with
details for the file formats
used in Tasword 2 and Softeknics
Wordmaster.

I am writing my own WP software,
and hope to write a conversion
utility for the above formats as
a separate program.

Can anyone tell me if I can sell
(or send into a mag. like this)
software written and compiled in
Hisoft PASCAL and tunes compiled
from Melbourne House's Music
Box?
            MIKE PIKE.

To Mike Pike from Brian Gaff

Firstly, yes you are indeed
correct about Bob Smith and the
Buccaneer mag.

If you really want to find out
about electronic component
suppliers, you should have a
look at a mag like Everyday
Electronics or Practical
Electronics. There are lots of
small companies about that can
sometimes beat the Maplin and
Greenweld prices!

The scanners that are used on
PCs usually have their own
interface. I myself, though
owning a PC, have never used a
scanner! I see from the ads

that their prices are dropping,
and indeed, there is now one
being produced for the PCW
range. It could well be possible
to adapt this one for use on
other Z80 machines.

Tasword 2 creates files that are
space-filled to 64 columns. In
other words, there are no
carriage returns and line feeds
as these are added at print
time.It's a very wasteful system
- most other WPs truncate lines
with CR/LF.

I thought the Softeknics (is
that the spelling?) product was
called The Writer? Wordmaster is
by PCG. However, I think they
are variations on the plain

Ascii file. The main differences
that I find in WP files are how
they insert control codes. This
can be a major headache, as most
companies do not give detailed
descriptions of their files.

Programs written with the aid of
other programs are a thorny
subject. If it's just for
magazine use, I would say there
is no problem. Indeed, in most
cases, if you mention that you
used a product on the loading
screen, that's all the supplier
asks.

I have certainly used HiSoft
Basic for some published
programs and that has been OK.
Melbourne House no longer exist,

as the name is now owned by Vir-
gin, so I think it very unlikely
that they would complain!

                         - B.G.

From Mr. K.J. Howard, ASHFORD

I am unable to get a print-out
of the pages as your information
sheet indicates that I should.
Maybe it is because my printer
set-up is not compatible with
any of the print options OUTLET
offers or maybe is is just me!

Whilst I have ZX Interface 1, my
printing system is a Centronics-
type Brother HR-5 printer via a
Tasman Interface with Tasman
Software of 652 bytes starting
at 64716.If I load in the Tasman
software before OUTLET then the
ZX Spectrum just stops as it
does if I BREAK into OUTLET and
then load in my software.
                  - K.J. Howard

To Mr. K.J. Howard From Brian C.

Yes, the problem is your set-up
is not compatible. Regrettably
it is not possible for OUTLET to
cover every single variation of
hardware and software but only
the most popular formats. Thus,
our Disciple print option means
just that - via the Disciple
Centronics port;the Interface 1
option is the RS232 port in that
device. However,you might try...

CLEAR 63999. Load OUTLET. BREAK.
Enter:9994 POKE 23607,60:RETURN.
Load the Tasman code. Alter line
1410 to initialize your Tasman
Interface to send print codes
(replace I'Face 1: OPEN #3;"B").
Run and test it! Let me know how
you get on.          - Brian C..

that their prices are dropping, and indeed, there is now one being produced for the PCW range. It could well be possible to adapt this one for use on other Z80 machines.

Tasword 2 creates files that are space-filled to 64 columns. In other words, there are no carriage returns and line feeds as these are added at print time.It's a very wasteful system - most other WPs truncate lines with CR/LF.

Ascii file. The main differences that I find in WP files are how they insert control codes. This can be a major headache, as most companies do not give detailed descriptions of their files.

Programs written with the aid of other programs are a thorny subject. If it's just for magazine use, I would say there is no problem. Indeed, in most cases, if you mention that you used a product on the loading screen, that's all the supplier asks.

Прежде всего, с Новым годом и всего

Я пишу в ответ на ваш Outletter в
январском номере, где вы спрашивали,
знает ли кто-нибудь надежный способ
обнаружения режима 128 после использования
POKE 23611, 205. Я знаю метод, который
должен сработать, но вам придется
протестировать его с подключенным
Interface 1, чтобы быть уверенным, так
как он может изменять «стандартную»
систему способами, о которых я не очень
много знаю.

Режимы 128 и 48 используют разные адреса
возврата при ошибке (на них указывают
системные переменные ERR SP 23613 и 4),
и PEEK по этому адресу должен показать
вам, в каком режиме вы находитесь. В 48
BASIC это обычно будет 4867 в ROM
(процедура MAIN-4), в то время как 128
BASIC использует процедуру «ONERR» в
буфере принтера.

На старых машинах 128 ONERR начинается
с 23325, в то время как на +2A и +3 она
находится на 23354, так что тест может
не только определить режим, но и быть
использован для установления того, какой
тип машины 128K используется. Это может
быть полезно, если вам нужно
использовать RAMDISK и т.д., где синтаксис
отличается.

Программы можно было бы писать для любой
машины 128K, используя оба типа синтаксиса
на разных строках и используя тест, чтобы
определить, на какую строку GO TO.

Если вы просто хотите проверить, какой
режим используется, все, что вам нужно
PEEKнуть — это старший байт адреса
возврата при ошибке, который будет 91 на
(всех) машинах 128K в режиме 128 (19 в
режиме 48). Чтобы определить тип 128
BASIC, PEEKните младший байт, который будет
29 для старой машины, 58 для +2A/+3.
Следующая строка, возможно, может быть
изящным способом проведения теста режима:-

  10 LET mode=48+80*(PEEK (PEEK 23613+256*
  PEEK 23614+1)=91)

Предыдущая строка BASIC просто присваивает
переменной MODE значение 128 или 48,
прямым образом указывая используемый режим.
Следующее было бы полезно, если у вас есть
программа, в которой вам нужно
использовать, скажем, RAMDISK на любой
машине 128K:

```text
100 LET type=PEEK(PEEK 23613+256*PEEK 23614):
IF type=29 THEN GO TO 120:REM older 128K machine

110 CAT "M:": SAVE "M:filename" CODE x,y:
GO TO 130

120 CAT !: SAVE !"filename" CODE x,y

130 RETURN
```

Единственная проблема с вышеуказанным в том,
что у вас могут возникнуть трудности при
вводе строки 120 на машине, которая
использует +3 BASIC! Однако я надеюсь, что
эта информация может быть вам полезна в
будущем. Если вы обнаружите, что у нее есть
какие-либо ограничения, я буду рад узнать,
но насколько я могу судить по своей
системе (серый +2 и без Interface 1), она
всегда работает нормально.
                - Miles Kinloch

Сканеры, применяемые на PC, обычно имеют собственный интерфейс. Сам я, хоть и владею PC, сканером отродясь не пользовался! Из рекламы я вижу, что цены на них падают, и более того — сейчас выпускается сканер для линейки PCW. Вполне возможно, удастся приспособить его и для других машин на Z80.

Tasword 2 создает файлы, дополненные пробелами ровно до 64 колонок. Иными словами, символов возврата каретки и перевода строки там нет — они добавляются прямо во время печати. Очень неэкономная система; большинство других текстовых процессоров просто обрезают строки с помощью CR/LF.

Мне казалось, продукт от Softeknics (так пишется?) назывался The Writer? Wordmaster — это разработка PCG. Впрочем, сдаётся мне, все они — лишь вариации обычного текстового ASCII-файла. Главное различие между файлами текстовых процессоров кроется во внедряемых управляющих кодах. И вот это может стать настоящей головной болью, поскольку большинство компаний не утруждает себя подробными описаниями структуры своих файлов.

Программы, созданные при помощи другого софта — тема щекотливая. Если речь идёт только о публикации в журнале, я бы сказал, что проблем никаких. Более того, в большинстве случаев авторам инструментов достаточно лишь упоминания их продукта на загрузочном экране.

Mr. K.J. Howard от Brian C.:

Да, проблема именно в несовместимости вашего оборудования. К сожалению, OUTLET не может охватить каждую существующую связку железа и софта, мы поддерживаем только самые популярные форматы. Поэтому наша опция печати Disciple означает строго печать через порт Centronics интерфейса Disciple, а опция Interface 1 подразумевает использование порта RS232 этого устройства. Тем не менее, вы можете попробовать следующее:

CLEAR 63999. Загрузите OUTLET. Нажмите BREAK.  
Введите: `9994 POKE 23607,60:RETURN`.  
Загрузите код Tasman. Измените строку 1410 так, чтобы инициализировать ваш Tasman Interface для отправки кодов печати (замените `I'Face 1: OPEN #3;"B"`).  
Запустите и проверьте! Дайте знать, как всё пройдёт.  
- Brian C.
